assigned.title: The screen the operator is looking at is the only one that cannot say what failed
assigned.acceptance:
THE SYMPTOM, FROM THE OPERATOR'S INSTALLED MSI AT f02703e. Windows package, desktop shell and CI all pass. The MSI installs, the native window opens, the bundled node starts, and the handshake completes -- liberty-sidecar-ready {"host":"127.0.0.1","port":62699}, followed by "catalog metadata source: none requested", which proves instrumentation ran to completion and the sidecar process is healthy. The window then displays:

  Project Liberty could not start this page
  Something failed before the application frame could render.

THAT TEXT IS apps/web/src/app/global-error.tsx, AND IT IS THE ONE SCREEN IN THIS APPLICATION THAT CANNOT SAY WHAT WENT WRONG. The component's signature was `{ reset }` -- it never declared Next's `error` argument, so the error was dropped at the parameter list. It logged nothing. It showed no digest. And its own comment said "The log has it", which was FALSE: nothing anywhere wrote it. Three rounds of Windows work were spent guessing at a failure that was reporting itself to nobody.

WHAT ITS PRESENCE ALREADY TELLS US, AND IT NARROWS THE PROBLEM A LOT. global-error renders only when the render fails at or above the root layout. For the operator to be looking at it, the window had ALREADY navigated to the sidecar origin, the document request had ALREADY passed the 403 request guard, and Next had ALREADY served HTML. So this is not PL-0753's class and not the shell's supervision path -- surface_failure drives the bundled splash, which contains none of this text. It is a render or hydration failure inside the application.

WHAT THIS TASK DOES NOT DO, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST SHAPE OF IT: it does not fix the render failure. The failure cannot be identified from this session. The packaged production artifact was booted here and GET / answers 200 with the real application -- the app shell, the skip link, the navigation including Browse, 2 inline scripts and 10 script tags all carrying a CSP nonce. So the defect does not reproduce on Linux from the same tree, and nothing records it on Windows. This task makes it RECORD ITSELF, which is the only thing that can end the guessing.

REQUIRED: THE BOUNDARY RECEIVES THE ERROR AND SURFACES THE DIGEST. The existing reasoning was half right -- a root-layout failure can carry a stack trace and a digest is the only thing safe to show. It then omitted the digest too. A digest is Next's own correlation id, lowercase hex, no message and no path; showing it is what lets an operator quote one line that matches a line in the log. When Next minted none, the page says so rather than leaving a blank where a reference should be.

REQUIRED: THE REPORT REACHES THE FILE THE OPERATOR ALREADY PASTES. The Rust shell captures the sidecar's stdout and stderr, redacts tokens, budget-caps the volume and writes %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.projectliberty.desktop\logs\sidecar.log. A browser-side failure had no route into it -- console.error in the page goes to the webview's console, which nothing captures. One POST to a local diagnostics route closes the gap and adds no file, no port and no new place to look.

REQUIRED: NO MESSAGE AND NO STACK CROSS THAT BOUNDARY. A message from a server component can carry a file path, a connection string, a query or a token; a stack carries build paths. The report is five bounded fields -- boundary, pathname with the query and fragment REMOVED, digest matched against lowercase hex, error name matched against an identifier pattern, and hadMessage as a BOOLEAN so a reader can tell an error that said nothing from one whose text was withheld. The server re-sanitises with the same rules rather than believing a body because it came from our own page.

REQUIRED: THE REPORTER CANNOT BE THE FAILURE. It is called from the last-resort boundary, which must not import the shell, the stylesheet, or anything that could be what just failed. The module imports NOTHING -- no React, no CSS, no contract package -- is total against anything JavaScript can throw including a throwing getter, and swallows every failure of its own.

REQUIRED: A REFUSAL LEAVES A TRACE. The request guard answers 403 with no body and no reason, deliberately, so the wire cannot be used as an oracle for which check failed -- and the consequence nobody accounted for is that a refusal left no trace ANYWHERE, which is why "does the installed WebView get 200 or 403" was unanswerable from the machine that served it. The wire is unchanged. The server-side log records the method, the path without its query, and whether a token header and a Host header were PRESENT -- no header value, and not which check failed. Between them those separate a webview that never attaches the token from one that attaches it to some requests and not others, from a Host mismatch, from a request that is not ours.

REQUIRED: BOTH LOGS ARE BUDGETED. One refused page load is dozens of refusals and a remount loop reports continuously; the line that matters is the first one. The budget keeps the first few per window, drops the rest, and says once per window how many it dropped -- so the log states that it stopped recording rather than appearing to say the failures stopped.

MUST NOT: weaken the request guard, change what the wire says, widen what the 403 reveals, or record any header value, token, query string or user data.

MUST NOT: claim the startup failure is fixed. It is not diagnosed. What this earns is that the next MSI run will say what failed, in the file the operator already sends.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-11 from the Wave 131 operator report. Two recon findings were checked and REJECTED before this was written: that the packaged proxy fails to forward a CSP nonce (the live packaged response carries a nonce on all 12 script tags), and that the homepage is served as an error page on Linux (it is the real application, 200). Both came from subagent reads of prerendered build output rather than of a live response. WAVE 132: surface widened by two modules and one gate added, deliberately. The frame-capture work added to the report two fields that cross a diagnostic boundary the task's own acceptance had closed (`shape`, derived from the message; `frames`, derived from the stack), so `security-review` is now required rather than trusted. network-state.ts and reachability-store.ts were added because the browser measurement named them: the frame the new capture produced resolved to an unguarded `navigator.onLine` in observeBrowser, forty lines below a guarded reader it did not use. Shipping a diagnostic for that class while leaving the measured instance in place would have been absurd.

typecheck.evidence:
TYPECHECK and UNIT at b14848c4978f96d8ae700158fdc95a885f09f1f5, FOURTH IMPLEMENTATION ROUND. The subject is the diagnostic's own information gap, measured against the operator's installed MSI at faa6e8a.

THE REPORT CAME BACK WITH shape "unclassified", AND THAT WAS MY DEFECT, NOT AN ENGINE ODDITY. The only pattern for a property access read "cannot read properties of". Chromium's write form -- "Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'x')" -- is a different defect with a different fix and matched nothing, and so did eight other forms a module-evaluation failure produces. The classifier shipped last round could name five shapes; a module-evaluation TypeError is usually none of them.

WHAT THE FRAMES ESTABLISHED FIRST, because the classifier change only matters given this. The three turbopack offsets in the operator's report resolve, in my copy of turbopack-32dm7-rex-nuz.js, to exactly: 2868 esmImport/namespaceObject, 7016 getOrInstantiateModuleFromParent, 7475 the module factory invocation inside its try/catch. Three independent offsets landing on the precise operations of one call chain in a 10844-byte minified file is not coincidence. So the throw is at MODULE-EVALUATION time, before any React render -- which is why the boundary is global-error with a null digest, and which rules out the render/hydration class pursued since round 130.

THREE FIELDS ADDED, AND THE SECOND ONE MOVES A BOUNDARY DELIBERATELY.
  shape: 13 forms, with the WRITE form ordered before the read form so the two stay distinguishable rather than one swallowing the other.
  detail: the ONE identifier the message names. The argument for admitting it: every message of this class names exactly one thing, and that thing is a JavaScript identifier from our own public bundle -- not user data. It is validated against the same bare-identifier pattern an error name is, so a path, a URL, a query string, a connection string, a quoted phrase with a space, a hyphenated name and an over-long name all become null. Asserted over seven such shapes, including "postgres://user:pw@host/db", a D:\ build path and "/api/v1/catalog?token=sekrit".
  messageLength: a number. It leaks nothing and it separates "this build could not classify the message" from "there was no message".

A WAVE 132 TEST FAILED ON THIS CHANGE AND WAS RIGHT TO FAIL. It asserted that the property named in a message appeared nowhere in the serialisation -- the boundary as the previous round drew it. Rather than delete it, it now states the boundary as it stands: a bare identifier MAY travel; no sentence fragment, host, scheme or path may. The check working is the reason the widening is recorded rather than silent. Two further failures were my own stale expectations, one of which tripped on the word "undefined" occurring inside a shape NAME -- a false positive I corrected rather than shipped as a rule.

TESTS: npx vitest run --root apps/web src/lib/diagnostics/client-failure.test.ts -- 48 passed (was 40). New coverage pins: the operator's exact write form classifying as undefined_property_write with detail "toString"; eleven engine messages across ten shapes; read and write staying distinct; the seven non-identifier shapes detail must refuse; totality over null/undefined/number/object/array/Symbol; a 3000-character message bounded; the server re-validating detail and messageLength rather than believing the body; and the on-screen reference line, which now reads "global-error · TypeError · undefined_property_write · toString · <chunk>:31:41369" so a photograph of the window is as useful as the log.

WHOLE SUITE at this commit: npx vitest run --root apps/web -- 127 files, 2558 tests, all passing. npm run test (turbo, whole repository) exit 0.

TYPECHECK: npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web clean. npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build (turbo, whole repository) all exit 0. ai:validate 170 tasks / 9 agents; test-ai-control-plane, validate-repo, test-validate-repo, notices, runs-nowhere, validate-env --scope ci all exit 0. build:desktop and package-sidecar exit 0, with the 20 external-link policy tests and the 7-check packaged smoke passing -- so the diagnostic survives production bundling, which is the only property that matters for a field whose job is to appear in an installed build's log.

ONE SUITE FAILED AND WAS A RACE, NOT A DEFECT: test-ai-control-plane exited 1 on the first gate pass because I wrote control/tasks.json while that suite held a snapshot of it. Re-run on the stable tree: exit 0. Recorded rather than quietly re-run.

NOT CLAIMED: that the startup failure is fixed. It is not diagnosed. In MY build the named offset resolves to a var-hoisted namespace assignment that cannot throw on a compliant engine, so either the operator's chunk is not byte-identical to mine or something evaluated before it mutated the environment. Byte identity is UNVERIFIED -- the folder-access request for the installed application timed out unanswered -- and treating the offset as authoritative without it would be the assumption the brief forbids. security-review remains outstanding and is deliberately not recorded here; this round widened what crosses the boundary, which makes that review more necessary, not less.

assigned.title: There is no way to browse the catalog: home shows two rails and search needs you to know the answer
assigned.acceptance:
THE GAP. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md names "Home/catalog/search" among the MVP capabilities. Home and search exist; there is no catalog surface. Browsing is currently two home rails -- RAIL_DEFINITIONS in lib/catalog.ts, films and series, newest first -- plus a search box that requires the viewer to already know what they are looking for. A viewer who wants to see what is in the catalog, or everything in one genre, has nowhere to go. /browse, /catalog, components/browse and any live-TV route do not exist in apps/web/src/app.

REQUIRED: A BROWSE SURFACE THAT READS THE SAME PORT THROUGH THE SAME GATES. The catalog metadata port (lib/catalog-source-registry.ts), then selectDeclaredItems, then isSurfaceable, then the browsable-kind allowlist -- the order home and search both already apply, and in that order, so a record whose rights basis the source did not declare is never reachable from this surface either. No new provider, no new fixture, no second catalog read path.

REQUIRED: THE FACETS ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT SURVIVED THE RIGHTS GATE, NOT FROM THE RECORDS. A genre list is published to the reader. Deriving it before the gate would let a withheld record contribute a genre name -- disclosing that the catalog holds something of that kind while refusing to show it, which is a rights leak through a filter control rather than through a card. The facet list must be computed from the surfaced items only, and a test must pin that ORDERING. The test needs a cast to do it, and the cast is itself the finding: contentRightsSchema admits only the three playable values, so every schema-valid CatalogItem is surfaceable and the union cannot express a withheld one -- the real withholding happens upstream in selectDeclaredItems, which refuses a record before it becomes an item at all. The ordering is still load-bearing against the rights vocabulary being widened later, which is the only way it can regress, and the test says so rather than implying the type system proves it.

REQUIRED: 'YOUR FILTERS MATCHED NOTHING' AND 'THE CATALOG HAS NOTHING' ARE DIFFERENT PAGES. This is the collapse app/search/search.ts documents at length and lib/catalog.ts carries a cause field for. An empty browse result must say which of the two it is, and the cause must come from the catalog rather than be inferred from the length of a filtered array, because both states legitimately produce an empty array.

REQUIRED: DETERMINISTIC ORDER WITH A FINAL TIEBREAK, AND NO localeCompare. Same catalog and same filters in, same list out, on any host. localeCompare without an explicit locale uses the host's collation, which is the defect already removed from candidate ranking in @liberty/media-engine and from search's result sort; buildHomeCatalog still has it and is not this task's surface. id decides last, so the sort can never fall back on the order the catalog arrived in.

REQUIRED: THE FILTERS LIVE IN THE URL AND WORK WITHOUT JAVASCRIPT. A GET form and search params, so a filtered view is shareable and bookmarkable and so the surface is complete before hydration. Parameters arrive as untrusted input and are read defensively: a repeated parameter takes its first value rather than being joined, an unrecognised value falls back to the unfiltered default, and nothing malformed produces a 500 -- the rules readSearchQueryParam already states for q.

REQUIRED: THE NAVIGATION ENTRY, AND A GUARD THAT THE PROMISE IN THAT FILE IS KEPT. navigation.ts's header says "every entry goes somewhere that exists" and nothing checks it: the existing test only asserts that a live href starts with a slash. A live entry whose route file is absent is exactly the dead link that file was written to remove, so the guard must resolve each live href to a page under apps/web/src/app and fail when one is missing.

MUST NOT: add a play affordance to a browse card, imply a resolvable stream from an item being visible, or weaken any rights gate. Browse is discovery; a stream is resolved through authorized provider adapters at playback time.

MUST NOT: add an HTTP contract or a route handler. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md requires schemas in @liberty/contracts before a route exists, and it lists no browse route among the planned contracts. This value is computed in the server render and nothing transports it, so a wire contract would be contract machinery with no transport. GET /api/v1/search is the planned route that would change that, and it is not this task.

MUST NOT: claim e2e coverage that was not run. The Playwright suite cannot be executed in this session; the surface is covered by vitest, the route is reachable through the navigation guard, and the e2e spec is deliberately left to a task that can run it rather than shipped unexecuted into a 45-minute job.

REQUIRED, ADDED MID-IMPLEMENTATION AND DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN QUIETLY: a brittle count in a test that is not this surface's must become the property it stands for. apps/web/src/components/profiles/profile-ui.test.tsx asserts PRIMARY_NAVIGATION has LENGTH 5 to mean "identity is not a content destination", and the line beside it already asserts that properly by checking /profiles is absent. The count is a proxy that fails on every legitimate nav addition -- it failed on this one -- and replacing it with the property removes a false alarm without removing a guard. The file was added to allowedPaths for this and nothing else; the /profiles assertion stays.

unit.evidence:
UNIT at 541ea53bb509d2cea9e063a80118e1269cf7d1ac, SECOND IMPLEMENTATION ROUND. npx vitest run --root apps/web src/app/browse/browse.test.ts src/components/browse/browse-filters.test.tsx src/components/shell/shell-usage.test.ts and their consumers: 6 files, 203 tests (was 104 before this wave). Whole suite: 127 files, 2548 tests, all passing. tsc clean, eslint 0 errors.

WHAT WAVE 132 ADDED TO THE SURFACE 131B SHIPPED, and it is an extension rather than a rebuild -- browseCatalog, the facet counting, the rights gate ordering and the deterministic sort tail are all unchanged and still have their original tests.

(1) SORTING. BrowseSortKey (newest, oldest, title, title-desc) with SORT_COMPARATORS that are each TOTAL and share one title-then-id tail. Rotation invariance is asserted per comparator: the same items in a different incoming order produce the same output order, which a partial comparator does not give you. Code point only -- no localeCompare anywhere, because a locale-dependent comparison makes the order a property of the machine rather than of the data.

(2) GENRE FILTERING rides the facet counts that were already computed after the gates, so a filter cannot surface an item the rights gate excluded and cannot show a count the gate did not produce.

(3) buildBrowseHref OMITS THE DEFAULT ORDER, so a shared URL carries no redundant state, and the round trip (href -> readBrowseFilters -> href) is asserted over ALL 108 combinations across /browse, /movies and /tv.

(4) shell-usage.test.ts now RESOLVES DYNAMIC SEGMENTS, so /title/[titleId] counts as existing; its rule that every live nav href must resolve to a real page.tsx keeps meaning what it says, and the non-vacuity assertion added in 130B is still there.

A PROBE EXPECTATION OF MINE WAS WRONG IN 131B AND IS RECORDED HERE AGAIN because it is the kind of thing that turns into a false bug report: I first asserted the filter controls were present on /browse, /movies and /tv and reported three failures. The controls were correctly ABSENT -- with no catalogue source the surface renders the unavailable panel. My expectations were wrong, not the code.

NEW INFORMATION FOR THIS TASK'S REVIEWER, MEASURED THIS WAVE. The reason these surfaces render the unavailable panel on the installed build is now established by driving the packaged artifact in a browser: its stdout says "catalog metadata source: none requested (set LIBERTY_CATALOG_SOURCE_ID to configure one)" and GET /api/v1/profiles answers 503 storage_not_configured because DATABASE_URL is unset. Neither variable is set anywhere in apps/desktop. That is filed as PL-0766 and is an architecture decision, not a defect in this task -- but it means the browse surface cannot be qualified against real data on the installed product until PL-0766 is decided.

Surface narrowed before claim: the declaration originally named components/state, components/catalog-card.tsx, components/catalog-rail.tsx and components/continue-watching, and the implementation changed none of them -- it consumes them. components/state additionally overlapped PL-0759, whose surface grew to cover the reachability store. A declaration wider than the work is a reservation against other lanes for nothing, which is what blocked this claim.
assigned.title: The home hero is a hard-coded sentence, so the first screen cannot say what this installation actually has
assigned.acceptance:
THE DEFECT. The home hero was a fixed marketing sentence and a single generic error line. On the installed Windows build -- which has no catalog metadata source -- that produced a first screen which stated a promise and could not state a fact, and an error state which could not distinguish "no source is configured" from "the source failed" from "the source returned nothing". A first screen that cannot describe the installation is the same defect class this project keeps finding: a shape standing in for a presence.

REQUIRED: THE HERO IS LOADER-DRIVEN AND TOTAL. Every reachable catalog state -- populated, each distinct empty cause, each distinct error reason -- renders a hero, and exactly one h1 in every one of them. Selection must be deterministic with explicit tie-breaks and must not use localeCompare, which is locale-dependent and therefore not an order.

REQUIRED: THE ERROR COPY NAMES THE REASON. One panel per reason the loader can actually return, so the operator reads a cause rather than "something went wrong". A reason the loader cannot return must not have a panel, and a reason it can return must not be missing one -- the test is a table over the loader's own union, so adding a reason without copy fails a test that names the dependency.

REQUIRED: RAIL KEYBOARD TRAVERSAL IS TESTABLE. apps/web/vitest.config.ts is environment: "node" with no jsdom and no app-router context, so a client component that renders next/link cannot be rendered in a test. The traversal logic therefore lives in a plain module and is tested directly; the client component is a thin consumer asserted by source rules. Do not add jsdom and do not mock Next internals to get around this.

REQUIRED: NO INVENTED AVAILABILITY. A "Recently Added" rail may only exist if the catalog contract carries a field that supports recency. It does not -- CatalogItem carries releaseYear and no ingestion date -- so no such rail may be added and no copy may call anything new or recent.

MUST NOT: redesign the approved interface, hand-roll the shell chrome in a route, or remove a page's own <AppShell> (shell-usage.test.ts enforces that each page-like file carries it, and that rule must keep meaning what it says).

MUST NOT: throw at module-evaluation time, or touch a non-universal browser API without a typeof guard. The installed WebView2 build is currently failing on a client TypeError and a new unguarded global would be indistinguishable from it.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: Wave 132 ran nine workstreams in parallel from this commit; all five implementations were written, tested and committed before any of these tasks was filed, because the tasks were derived from the finished disjoint surfaces rather than the reverse. 62c88fa is the branch tip at which every worker started and the last commit before any Wave 132 code exists.

AND IT COMPILES AS A BUILD, NOT ONLY AS TYPES: npm run build:desktop -w @liberty/web completed and apps/desktop/scripts/package-sidecar.mjs laid out the packaged tree from it, which is the check that matters for a route that type-checks but does not register.

unit.evidence: UNIT at 541ea53bb509d2cea9e063a80118e1269cf7d1ac. npx vitest run --root apps/web: 127 files, 2548 tests, all passing. The suite moved from 100 files / 1772 tests at the 131B tip to 127 / 2548 across Wave 132; this task contributes 59 in src/components/home (spotlight.test.ts, rail-navigation.test.ts, home-ui.test.tsx). WHAT THE TESTS PIN. (1) EXACTLY ONE h1 IN EVERY REACHABLE STATE -- populated, each empty cause and each error reason -- because the defect being removed is a first screen that could not describe the installation, and a state with no heading or two headings is that defect in a different shape. (2) THE ERROR COPY IS A TABLE OVER THE LOADER'S OWN UNION, so a reason the loader can return and the panel table cannot name fails a test that says which dependency moved; the loader currently publishes three reasons and there are four panels including the fallback. (3) SPOTLIGHT SELECTION IS DETERMINISTIC with an explicit tie-break chain (releaseYear desc, title by code point, id) and no localeCompare anywhere -- a rotation-invariance test asserts the same winner from a rotated input list. (4) THE SKELETON RESERVES HOME_RAIL_KINDS.length RAILS, not one, which was a visible layout shift. assigned.title: Search ranks by a four-value enum, so the result a viewer wanted can sort below one that merely contains the word
assigned.acceptance:
THE DEFECT. Search classified each hit into one of four kinds and sorted by that classification alone. Two hits with the same kind had no defined order between them beyond the list's incoming order, and a word-boundary match -- the single most common thing a person means when they type two letters -- was indistinguishable from a match buried inside a longer word.

REQUIRED: A REAL RELEVANCE ORDER, COMPUTED LOCALLY AND DETERMINISTICALLY. Tiers from exact through prefix and word-prefix to substring, weighted by field with title ahead of the rest, and a total comparator whose tail is the catalog's existing deterministic order (releaseYear desc, then title by code point, then id). No localeCompare and no toLocaleLowerCase anywhere in an ordering path: a locale-dependent comparison makes the order a property of the machine.

REQUIRED: THE SCORER CANNOT THROW AT EVALUATION TIME AND CANNOT BE BUILT FROM THE QUERY. A RegExp compiled from user input is an injection and a denial-of-service surface; a Unicode property escape that an older engine rejects at parse time takes the whole module down. Both are structurally excluded, and the fallback path is tested rather than assumed.

REQUIRED: AN HONEST AVAILABILITY LINE. The surface may report only what the rights gate actually read off the item -- never "available" or "playable", which it has not established. The function that produces it is total and has an explicit refused branch.

REQUIRED: MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, DE-DUPLICATION. A request-scoped memo must be proven by counters that the test reads, not by a comment claiming a cache exists. It must single-flight on the promise, must cache a null result, and must never cache a rejection.

MUST NOT: add a contract field that nothing can populate. Where the published match-kind enum is coarser than the internal order, report that as a contract change to be decided -- do not widen the enum silently.

assigned.title: Watchlist, history, resume and preferences are four unrelated reads, so switching profile switches some of them
assigned.acceptance:
THE DEFECT. Per-viewer state was reached through several independent reads with no single notion of whose state it is, so there was no one place that could answer "is this snapshot the active profile's" and no one place a reset could act on. A failed read answered with an empty list, which is indistinguishable from a profile that genuinely has nothing -- an absence standing in for a presence, again.

REQUIRED: ONE SNAPSHOT, ONE PORT, AND A FAILED READ THAT SAYS SO. Watchlist, favourites, Continue Watching, history and resume positions are one coherent per-profile model behind a narrow persistence port. A failed read answers null, never an empty collection, and staleness against the active profile is a value the caller can read rather than a thing it must infer. No port method takes a profile id: scope is derived server-side, so a caller cannot ask for someone else's state.

REQUIRED: PREFERENCES ARE VERSIONED AND THE MIGRATION IS TOTAL. A stored record written by an older build must never crash a newer one. The migration accepts anything, including a record of the wrong shape, and the test asserts that over hostile input rather than over the happy path.

REQUIRED: DELETION IS VERIFIED BY RE-READ, NOT BY STATUS CODE. A 204 proves a request was accepted, not that data is gone. Each reset that is implemented re-reads and asserts absence; each reset that is NOT implemented refuses honestly and names what it cannot remove. A control that appears to delete and does not is worse than no control.

REQUIRED: NO BROWSER STORAGE, STILL. This application deliberately uses no localStorage and no sessionStorage, and two existing tests enforce it. Persistence goes through the server-side repository.

REQUIRED: THE TWO UNGUARDED MODERN APIs ON THIS SURFACE ARE GUARDED. Intl.Segmenter is constructed and destructured in the avatar path and Object.hasOwn is read in the watchlist path; both run inside the application shell on the installed WebView2 build that is currently failing with a client TypeError. Guard the property access itself, the construction, and the destructuring -- the iterator is a separate failure point from the constructor -- and make the fallback correct for astral characters rather than returning a lone surrogate.

MUST NOT: introduce an account system, a cloud dependency or a sync service. MUST NOT fabricate a favourites feature: if there is no store for it, report not-implemented.

recommended.title: The homepage loads shaka-player and 112 KB of vendored core-js, and has no player on it
recommended.acceptance:
MEASURED ON 2026-10-13 by booting the packaged artifact built from faa6e8a and reading the homepage's own script tags, in document order:

   1 0uqxvrcch5o_0.js      6 2ic50n3d1m9j1.js   <- Zod + components/profiles/avatar.ts
   2 1oml7c7env4-g.js      7 1eoo6bbg-tei8.js
   3 turbopack-...js       8 0e3rt6sy81x-m.js
   4 2kio16qodpvga.js      9 0cz1d0mv5g_q7.js   <- shaka-player + vendored core-js, 112594 bytes
   5 3hvn4kknuhx97.js     10 2mmpezlrfmbu5.js

TWO LEAKS INTO THE CLIENT STARTUP PATH, NEITHER OF WHICH THE HOMEPAGE USES.

(1) SHAKA-PLAYER AND ITS VENDORED core-js. `npm ls core-js` reports nothing and no repository source imports it; shaka-player declares it and ships it inlined. core-js does FEATURE DETECTION AND BUILT-IN PATCHING AT MODULE-EVALUATION TIME -- the chunk contains `__core-js_shared__`, RegExp named-group and dotAll probes, and Object.defineProperty writes against built-ins. The homepage has no player on it. 112 KB of polyfill that patches globals is evaluated on every page load of an application whose target engine needs none of it.

(2) ZOD IN A CLIENT CHUNK. Chunk 6 carries Zod's full runtime beside our own avatar module, which means a client component reaches `@liberty/contracts`. The contracts package is a server-side validation boundary; its presence in the browser is a bundle-graph leak, and it is the chunk the Wave 132 crash frame points into.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN THE SAME ROUND. It is NOT established that either leak causes the Wave 132 startup failure, and saying so would be the unsupported claim the brief forbids. Document order puts the core-js chunk AFTER the chunk the crash frame names, so core-js cannot have mutated the environment before that chunk evaluated. What is established is that both are real defects of their own, on the startup path, in the installed product.

THE DECISION REQUESTED: whether the player is moved behind a dynamic import so shaka and its polyfill load only on a watch route, and whether `@liberty/contracts` gains a client-safe entry point that carries types without Zod's runtime. Both change the module graph of a product whose packaging has been fragile for five rounds, which is why they are a decision rather than a patch.

MUST NOT: be used as evidence for a cause that has not been demonstrated, and MUST NOT be bundled into a P0 startup-recovery release.
